questions.prompt: What scope of fix do you want?
questions.description: The current clj-edit (rewrite-clj) exists but you said 'it does not work properly'. There are also zero tools for non-Clojure files. Pick which problems this goal should address.
questions.recommendedAnswer: All three: improve the existing clj-edit tool (add missing ops, fix real-world reliability, sharpen descriptions), add a general file tool for non-Clojure files, and add system-prompt guidance so the LLM actually picks the right tool.

options.label: Improve existing clj-edit tool (missing ops, reliability, descriptions)
Add a general file-edit tool for non-Clojure files (.py, .md, .toml, etc.)
System-prompt / tool-description guidance so the LLM picks the right tool

questions.prompt: Which clj-edit operations are missing or broken?
questions.description: Existing 6 ops: read-structure, find-form, replace-form, insert-form, add-require, remove-form. What should be added or fixed?
questions.recommendedAnswer: rename-form (preserves docstring/attrs), edit-form-body (in-place body replace without losing metadata), move-form (relocate a form to a different position), and stricter error messages when a form name is ambiguous or doesn't exist. Also fix the documented bug where clj-paren-repair mangles (cond (pred? x) val) — but that lives in clj-paren-repair, not here.

options.label: rename-form — change a defn's name in place, preserving docstring/attrs
edit-form-body — replace only the body of a defn, preserve metadata/args
move-form — relocate a form to after a different form
Better error messages for ambiguous / missing form names

questions.prompt: What operations should a general file tool expose?
questions.description: Design the API for the non-Clojure file tool. Should be minimal — LLM will compose these into edits.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Five ops: read_file (path → contents with optional offset/limit), write_file (path → full overwrite, refuses if path looks like a Clojure file unless explicit), edit_file (path + old_text + new_text, the classic str-replace but with validation that old_text exists exactly once), list_dir (path → entries), and show_diff (path + new_contents → unified diff). edit_file must reject ambiguous matches (old_text appears 0 or >1 times) with a structured error so the LLM can adapt.

options.label: read_file — read a file, with optional offset/limit for large files
write_file — create or fully overwrite a file
edit_file — find unique old_text, replace with new_text (the Edit tool pattern)
list_dir — list directory entries
show_diff — show unified diff before applying a change

questions.prompt: How should the agent decide which file tool to use?
questions.description: A Clojure file ending in .clj/.cljs/.cljc/.edn should go through clj-edit. Everything else through the general tool. How is that enforced?
questions.recommendedAnswer: By tool description: the general file tool's :description explicitly says 'For Clojure/EDN files, use clj_edit instead.' clj_edit's :description says it's the preferred tool for Clojure. The write_file op refuses .clj/.cljs/.cljc/.edn paths with a structured error pointing at clj_edit. The system prompt (or equivalent) reinforces: 'For Clojure file changes that should persist, prefer clj_edit over repl-eval.'

options.label: Tool descriptions gate which tool to use for which file type, plus system-prompt hint
General tool hard-refuses Clojure files; clj_edit hard-refuses non-Clojure
A single 'edit' tool that auto-routes to clj-edit or general based on file extension

questions.prompt: What safety constraints should the file tools have?
questions.description: Both tools write to disk. What's the safety surface?
questions.recommendedAnswer: write_dir constraint (only write under an allowed directory, default $cwd), reject writes to common sensitive paths (.git, target/, .clojure-mcp-light/, node_modules/), and require a confirmation flag for writes outside write_dir. No undo/rollback in v1 (defer).

options.label: write_dir constraint (configurable; only writes under allowed root)
Block writes to .git, target/, node_modules/, etc.
Require a :force flag for writes outside write_dir
Auto-backup before each write so a rollback fn can revert

questions.description: How should we verify the new behavior end-to-end?
questions.recommendedAnswer: All four: per-op unit tests for new clj-edit ops; per-op unit tests for the general file tool; a parity/scenario test that runs the agent through a multi-step Clojure refactor (add-require → find-form → edit-form-body) and asserts the file on disk matches; an integration test that verifies the general file tool correctly refuses a Clojure path with a 'use clj_edit' error.

options.label: Unit tests for each new clj-edit operation
Unit tests for each general file tool operation (incl. edit_file ambiguity)
Multi-step parity: scripted LLM refactor scenario through clj_edit ops
Integration: general file tool refuses .clj with a 'use clj_edit' error

questions.recommendedAnswer: No changes to repl-eval (it stays as the in-memory / one-off tool per your direction). No LLM-side self-modification protocol changes. No rewrite of the existing 6 clj-edit ops (we add to them, not rewrite). No sandboxing / OS-level isolation.

options.label: Do not touch repl-eval — it stays as-is
No changes to the self-modification protocol
Don't rewrite the existing 6 clj-edit ops; only add new ones
No OS-level sandboxing (no firejail, no seccomp, no chroot)
